paths.description: Homepage/listing template: purpose, search, catalogue, preferences, mobile reflow, performance, security, accessibility, discoverability, and memory.
Representative movie detail template: metadata, content hierarchy, imagery, breadcrumbs, primary download action, mobile reflow, and no-JS visibility.
POST search with a deliberately absent title: empty-state messaging, preserved context, and retry control.
Unknown-route HTTP failure: status correctness and recovery affordances.
Primary catalogue journey from a detail CTA to available file choices; stopped before fetching any media file.

findings.summary: The site remains hard-coded light when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The dark/reduced-motion screenshot is pixel-identical to the default screenshot; DOM computed styles remain a white body with color-scheme: normal and there is no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens for surfaces, text, borders, and form controls.

findings.summary: Page changes are abrupt and do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition-name, @view-transition, or transition CSS; the site is a server-rendered MPA with ordinary navigations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin listing-to-detail navigation, with reduced-motion handling and a no-transition fallback.

findings.summary: The very long listing offers no position-aware navigation or progress affordance.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout is 6,635px tall, while screenshots and CSS show no sticky header, progress indicator, back-to-top control, scroll-state query, or equivalent.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight position-aware back-to-top or shrinking navigation affordance using scroll-state queries where supported, progressively enhanced.

findings.summary: Repeated SEO copy and keyword-heavy footer content push the actual catalogue behind non-task content.
findings.evidence: The first mobile viewport is dominated by a 400px generic SEO introduction; the detail DOM repeats it before each title and ends with a long keyword tag dump and repeated heading links.
findings.suggestedFix: Lead with search and catalogue/detail content, move concise context below it, and remove repeated keyword stuffing and duplicated footer headings.

findings.summary: The primary search controls are too small for reliable touch use.
findings.evidence: The platform probe measured the text input at 181x19px and Search submit at 58x21px; both are well below the commonly expected 44px touch height, although keyboard focus remains visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Give search controls at least a 44x44 CSS-pixel hit area, preserve visible :focus-visible styling, and retain the explicit label.

findings.summary: The 404 state has no useful recovery path.
findings.evidence: The server correctly returns HTTP 404, but the mobile screenshot only shows “404 Not Found” and tiny “nginx” text on an otherwise blank page, with no home, search, or retry action.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the normal site shell with a clear explanation, search field, home/category links, and a retained 404 status.

findings.summary: At least one text treatment misses WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found the green “Tag:” text at 4.1:1 against #dde7f1, below the required 4.5:1 for 13px bold text; accessibility score was 0.94.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a darker green or a lighter background so normal-size text reaches at least 4.5:1, and verify all dynamic color classes.

findings.summary: Small search targets weaken reflowed and touch use.
findings.evidence: At the 360px mobile viewport there is no horizontal overflow and scaling is allowed, but the search input and submit control are only 19px and 21px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive control hit areas to at least 44px while preserving fluid reflow and user zoom.

findings.summary: The document relies on obsolete presentational markup and repeated inline CSS.
findings.evidence: Rendered HTML uses center, font, align, width percentages in attributes, nested headings, and repeats the full .seo-header style block; the doctype and charset themselves are valid.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace presentational elements/attributes with semantic HTML and consolidate repeated styles into the external stylesheet.

findings.summary: robots.txt advertises a sitemap on an unrelated hostname.
findings.evidence: https://filmyifly.com/robots.txt says “Sitemap: https://tvdl.m1link.qzz.io/sitemap.xml”, while https://filmyifly.com/sitemap.xml exists and lists filmyifly.com sitemap indexes; canonicals use filmyifly.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Point robots.txt at the canonical filmyifly.com sitemap index and keep redirects, canonicals, and sitemap hosts consistent.

findings.summary: Homepage social preview image metadata is empty.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found og:image, og:image:secure_url, and twitter:image with empty content on the homepage; detail pages do provide a poster and Movie JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide an absolute branded social image URL with dimensions and alt text on the homepage.

findings.summary: The site omits core browser security headers.
findings.evidence: The final-domain header audit found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. HTTPS is used and no cookies or exposed secrets were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, strict-origin-when-cross-origin Referrer-Policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy; test before enforcement.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: Header evidence shows no clickjacking defense, referrer policy, permissions policy, HSTS, or CSP; this leaves the browser unable to enforce several baseline mitigations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add and monitor the defensive headers as one deployment task, beginning with report-only CSP if necessary.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling falls back to an unbranded server page.
findings.evidence: A real unknown route returns 404 but displays only a blank nginx error page, unlike the styled empty-search state that preserves context and recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve resilient branded 4xx/5xx templates with search and recovery actions while preserving correct HTTP status codes.

findings.summary: Mixed-language content is not marked up by language.
findings.evidence: The page declares html lang="en" but includes a prominent Hindi heading (“मूवी डाउनलोड कैसे करें!”) without lang="hi"; no hreflang variants are exposed and the inspected CSS contains no logical-property strategy.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark language changes with lang="hi", keep the document language accurate, and use logical CSS properties for future bidirectional/localized layouts.

findings.summary: Image delivery is light overall but still uses mostly legacy, non-responsive assets.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 53 of 54 images in PNG, no responsive srcset for the 1280px logo displayed at 400px, and one oversized image. The HAR remained a modest 116KB total.
findings.suggestedFix: Create appropriately sized AVIF/WebP variants and srcset/sizes for the logo and thumbnails while preserving explicit dimensions and lazy loading.
